items.title: Dutch privacy authority urges consumers not to buy 'pervert glasses'
items.excerpt: The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning they compromise bystanders' privacy, get information wrong and can create unsafe situations for wearers. Regulator action on AI smart glasses.
items.rationale: A national regulator formally telling consumers not to buy AI camera glasses is a new official action, and it bears on anyone buying or designing for the category. The cross-section brief assigns it to gadgets; the Korean bill goes to politics.

items.title: Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now
items.excerpt: Brain-computer interface company Paradromics is using Nvidia's computing hardware and software to process brain data.
items.rationale: New hardware partnership: Paradromics' Connexus BCI now processes neural data on Nvidia compute, bringing AI hardware into implantable interfaces. No BCI story appears in gadgets history or in the medicine and science URL lists that were checked.

items.title: I really wanted the Asus ProArt P14 to be my favorite RTX Spark laptop — and it's painfully close
items.excerpt: Tom's Guide reviews the Asus ProArt P14, an Nvidia RTX Spark 'portable AI studio' laptop: dazzling 3K OLED and 12.5-hour battery, but the slim chassis forces throttled wattage that runs hot under local-AI and creative loads.
items.rationale: This is today's single AI-PC laptop review. Of the three, it is the one aimed at creators, and it gives a hands-on verdict on whether the RTX Spark laptop handles local-AI and creative loads.

items.title: Copilot+ PCs: Why the NPU is no longer a reason to buy a laptop
items.excerpt: Many holiday laptop deals still carry the Copilot+ PC label, but the NPU barely sets devices apart anymore. Every new chip from AMD, Intel and Qualcomm clears 40 TOPS, Microsoft is quietly retiring the brand, and the most popular local AI apps don't use the NPU at all.
items.rationale: Practical buying guidance: Microsoft is quietly retiring the Copilot+ brand and local AI apps skip the NPU, so the label no longer tells buyers much. Published during holiday laptop shopping.

items.title: Flowtica Verso vs. Comulytic Note Pro: This one wins on speed - and price
items.excerpt: ZDNET compares two AI voice recorders, the Flowtica Verso (magnetic, always-on e-paper display) and the Comulytic Note Pro, on transcription speed, price and whether an AI recorder needs a screen.
items.rationale: A head-to-head test of two AI voice recorders on transcription speed and price. Neither device has appeared in history (the 11-13 card was Anker's Soundcore Work), and it gives a clear pick for meeting-notes hardware.
